title.narrative: Supporting MSMEs Competitiveness and Growth Programme
Utveckling av MSMEs konkurrenskraft och tillväxt

description.narrative: Det begärda programmet från Global Communities syftar till att utforma och genomföra ett 4-årigt, adaptivt och evidensbaserat utvecklingsprogram för marknadssystem som stärker konkurrenskraften och tillväxten för mikroföretag, små och medelstora företag (MSME) i Palestina, skapar anständiga jobb, särskilt för kvinnor och ungdomar, och bidrar till en motståndskraftig ekonomisk utveckling i Palestina. Det föreslås att Sverige stödjer genomförandet av programmet med 75 MSEK från november 2022 till november 2026. Denna period inkluderar en 10-månaders uppstartsfas. Bidraget bedöms vara relevant i förhållande till Sveriges strategi för internationellt utvecklingssamarbete med Palestina (2020-2024) , inom stödområdena "inkluderande ekonomisk utveckling" och "miljö och klimat". Det ligger också i linje med nationella palestinska strategier och prioriteringar. Programmet bidrar även till den gemensamma europeiska strategin (2021–2024) och Team Europe-initiativet (TEI) i Palestina. Det övergripande målet med bidraget är att förbättra de förutsättningar som krävs för ökad konkurrenskraft och tillväxt för mikroföretag samt små och medelstora företag, vilket bidrar till hållbar ekonomisk utveckling (bättre inkomster), produktiv sysselsättning med anständiga arbetsvillkor för kvinnor och ungdomar. Bidraget kommer att ha en strategi för utveckling av marknadssystem för att bättre förstå de kritiska begränsningar för tillväxt som finns idag för mikroföretag samt små och medelstora företag och för att säkerställa en hållbar strategi för att hantera dessa begränsningar. Programmet ska på lång sikt bidra till att skapa arbetstillfällen, särskilt för kvinnor och ungdomar, och öka Palestinas ekonomiska oberoende. Programmet kommer förhålla sig till principer för anständigt där det är relevant. Programmet kommer också fokusera på privata sektorns roll när det gäller att stödja övergången till en grön ekonomi. Särskild uppmärksamhet kommer att riktas mot områden med det största antalet mikroföretag samt små och medelstora företag och geografiska områden som är särskilt utsatta, särskilt Gaza, Hebron, område C och östra Jerusalem. Sida bedömer att programmet har väl integrerat principerna om lokalt ägande och hållbarhet. Global Communities har dessutom integrerat deltagande och inkludering i programdesign och implementering. Programmet samverkar med relevanta nationella och multinationella organisationer som fokuserar på stöd till mikroföretag samt små och medelstora företag, utveckling av marknadssystem, tillgång till finansiering, anständiga arbetstillfällen, öka hushållens motståndskraft med fokus på människor som lever i fattigdom, samt inkludering av kvinnor och ungdomar i ekonomiska utvecklingsinsatser. Programmets förändringsteori och mål verkar rimliga och kommer sannolikt att uppnås. Bidraget kommer att omfatta en 10-månaders uppstartsfas för att genomföra djupgående analyser och förfina strategin och programdesignen baserat på lärdomar och kunskap om de hinder som finns för mikroföretag samt små och medelstora företags konkurrenskraft och tillväxt i olika geografiska områden. Global Communities kommer regelbundet att se över och uppdatera deras förändringsteori och resultatramverk med syfte att fördjupa sin kunskap om på hur jämställdhet, ungdomar och miljöfrågor kan integreras, anpassa insatserna därefter och följa upp detta för att öka chanserna att uppnå programmålen.

The requested program by Global Communities aims to design and implement a 4-year, adaptive and evidence-based market system development (MSD) program that strengthens the competitiveness and growth of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Palestine, creates decent jobs especially for women and youth and leads to a process of resilient economic development in Palestine. It is proposed that Sweden supports the implementation of the program with MSEK 75 during November 2022 to November 2026. This period includes a 10-month inception phase. The contribution is assessed to be relevant in relation to Sweden's International Development Cooperation Strategy with Palestine (2020-2024) namely the “inclusive economic development” and the “environment and climate” support areas. It is also in line with national Palestinian strategies and priorities. It also contributes to the European joint strategy (2021-2024) and Team Europe Initiative (TEI) in Palestine. The overall objective of the contribution is to improve the conditions necessary for increased competitiveness and growth of MSMEs, contributing to sustainable economic development (better incomes), productive employment with decent work conditions for women and youth. The contribution will have a market systems development approach to better understand the critical constraints to MSMEs growth that exist and to ensure a sustainable approach to addressing these constraints. Ultimately, the contribution will contribute to job creation especially for women and youth and increase Palestine’s economic independence. Principles of decent work will be considered in the program where relevant. Attention is also given to the role of the private sector in supporting the transition to a green economy. Particular attention will be directed to areas with highest numbers of MSMEs and highly deprived geographic areas, particularly Gaza, Hebron, Area C and East Jerusalem. It is assessed that principles of local ownership and sustainability are embedded in program design. GC’s approach to program design and implementation is inclusive and participatory. It also engages relevant national and multi-national organizations focused on MSMEs support, MSD, access to finance, decent job creation, building household resilience targeting the poor, and the inclusion of women and youth in economic development efforts. The ToC and associated objectives seem plausible and likely to be achieved. The contribution will include a 10-month inception phase to conduct in-depth analyses and refine program design and approach based on lessons learned and evidence on barriers to MSMEs’ competitiveness and growth in different geographic areas. GC will regularly challenge and update the ToC and results framework and focus on learning and adapting the interventions and will focus on how gender, youth and environmental issues will be integrated and monitored in order to increase the chances of achieving program objectives.

The overall objective of the Programme is to improve the conditions necessary for increased competitiveness and growth of micro, small and medium enterprise in Palestines, contributing to their sustainable income change (better incomes), and job creation for women and youth.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement Global Communities - Supporting MSMEs competitiveness and growth in Palestine
Decision on Contribution Supporting MSMEs competitiveness and growth Programme

description.narrative:
The first reporting period of "Supporting MSMEs Competitiveness and Growth Programme - SMCGP" implemented by Global Communities - GC, included a 10-month inception phase with the aim of setting up the program team, fine-tuning the program's vision, objectives, and anticipated outcomes, conducting a thorough research and assessment process, deciding on the potential economic sectors/market systems to be targeted, and designing intervention strategies in alignment with national priorities. This process included a high level of engagement from different stakeholders, including the program team, partners, MSMEs, representatives from both the public and private sectors, and other community members to ensure that the needs, preferences, and diverse experiences of all stakeholders are captured. All these efforts were aimed at developing a comprehensive evidence-based program design.
The following was mainly achieved during the inception phase:
Setting up program team and operational guides:
GC has become fully functional with the majority of key positions filled and program offices have been set-up. A comprehensive operational guide for the program has also been developed.
Forming program steering and advisory committees (program governance):
GC formed the Program Steering and Advisory Committees. The role of the Program Steering Committee will be to provide strategic advice and oversight and to assist the program in effectively and timely identifying and managing risks and opportunities. While the main role of the Program Advisory committee will be to provide strategic and need-based advisory support and to ensure coordination and synergies with other programs active in the MSME development sphere.
Developing a Collaboration, Learning & Adaptation (CLA) strategy:
GC developed the CLA strategy, which was an integral part of the inception phase to ensure that activities are based on sound and available evidence, generating knowledge and data for adaptive management.
Delivering Market System Development (MSD) training:
A three-day MSD training was conducted, targeting the GC team and partners. The training aimed to establish a foundational understanding of MSD that the team can further develop through program activities. Additionally, the training emphasized the importance of localizing this knowledge among local partners.
Selecting the program targeted sectors:
A thorough market systems prioritization and selection process was carried out, beginning with 30 sectors (14 in Gaza Strip and 16 in the West Bank) spanning active sectors in agriculture, manufacturing, and services. Selection criteria and matrix was established encompassing economic growth, inclusivity (demographic and geographic inclusivity), feasibility, and environmental impact (including green transition) to evaluate each sector. The process entailed a thorough and iterative research and assessment, highlighting each sector's potential, key constraints, and intervention feasibility. Sector selection subsequently narrowed down to 1 sector in the Gaza Strip and 1 sector in the West Bank to be mainly targeted in the program.
In the West Bank, SMCGP is focusing on the creative industries (footwear & leather, furniture and handicrafts industries), where the majority of enterprises are MSMEs. In the Gaza Strip, SMCGP plans to target the food sector (flour based, processed and preserved, and other food products) and hospitality/tourism sector (restaurants, coffee shops and coastal services), driven by strong market demand, active engagement of women and youth, and a significant number of MSMEs. These sectors constitute of~10,000 MSMEs employing ~40,000 people.
Conducting market systems assessment and proposing intervention strategies:
In addition to the overview analysis of all investigated sectors, a deep-dive market systems assessment (MSA) was conducted for the two targeted sectors. The MSA served as the primary foundation for designing the intervention strategies and proposing implementation and intervention partners.
Conducting stakeholder mapping & analysis:
A stakeholder mapping and analysis was conducted, covering relevant stakeholders within the sectors targeted by the program. This matrix will serve as a reference to enhance the understanding of potential partners' capacities and incentives. As the program progresses, it anticipates identifying additional potential stakeholders.
Developing a women & youth strategy:
An analysis on women and youth inclusion was conducted, focusing on major constraints and opportunities facing women and youth in the targeted market systems, as workers and entrepreneurs. The analysis served as a guide for women and youth mainstreaming within the intervention strategy to better address their specific barriers.
Developing a policy and influencing strategy:
A policy and influencing strategy was developed in which SMCGP highlighted the most critical regulatory gaps to be addressed through this program and proposed an intervention strategy.
Launching the Gaza Grant Facility and documenting case studies & lessons learnt from Gaza Strip:
The Gaza Grant Facility aims at supporting MSMEs in Gaza with grants through Palestine Investment Fund (PIF) Co-financing. 25 MSMEs (out of 500 applications received) were provided with grants to support their production. Two case studies were drafted to capture insights from two MSMEs in Gaza that received grants. The insights gathered from these case studies were incorporated into the design of the interventions.
Updating the Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Strategy:
Based on the updated program design, the MEL strategy has been revised, including updates to indicators, targets and data collection methodologies. Also, the Theory of Change (TOC) has been revised and updated, and a results chain has been drafted for each proposed intervention.
Updating risk analysis and mitigation strategy and exit strategy:
The risk register and mitigation strategy were updated using insights gained from the inception phase activities. The revised version offers a more comprehensive outline of potential risks, along with their corresponding mitigation strategies and contingency plans. Additionally, an exit strategy for the program at various levels, both programmatic and intervention-wise, has been developed to facilitate smooth phase-out for GC from the targeted market systems.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
